packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Transcribe what you can see, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure and method
I read only PROMPT.md, packet.json, and image-001.png. Tools used: exec_command (to read the two text inputs and write response.txt), view_image (detail: original), and the functions.exec wrapper. No network, catalogue, edition, other image, or earlier transcription was consulted. No proposed source identification or earlier reading was present in my supplied task context. I have not attempted to identify the work or author. The exact model identifier is not exposed to me.

Transcription
Line numbers count visible physical writing lines from the top, including the fragment clipped by the upper edge. A question mark marks an uncertain reading; square brackets describe image conditions or illegibility. The macron in cō represents a visible abbreviation stroke approximately, not an exact reproduction of its shape. Parenthetical expansions are proposals only.

image-001.png:1 [illegible; only the lower portions of a line are visible at the upper edge]
image-001.png:2 Et? [illegible] [possibly an abbreviation stroke] [illegible]
image-001.png:3 In generacōe (generacione?) enim requiruntur? virtutes? actiua et passiua
image-001.png:4 [illegible] actiue? quasi contraria? eadem? diuisa? In generacōe (generacione?)
image-001.png:5 enim hominis virtus actiua est in viro Passiua vero
image-001.png:6 in muliere Ideo datur adiutorium [overwritten/corrected letters, perhaps et?] adiutor? con
image-001.png:7 tra? virū (virum?) [illegible] propria? passiuam? contrarie? a? actio?
image-001.png:8 Et ex? [illegible] et mulier fuit eiusdem speciei [illegible; cropped at bottom]

Visible corrections and layout
A dark tangle of strokes after “adiutorium” on line 6 appears to contain correction or overwriting. A heavy short horizontal stroke sits beneath or across the preceding letter group. I cannot reliably separate an original reading from a replacement. The following “adiutor?” also has crowded strokes. I do not assign a definite deletion or added word to these marks.
There is a short dark horizontal mark above the latter part of “virū?” on line 7, compatible with an abbreviation mark. There are also small marks above the later words of line 7 whose function is uncertain. The abbreviation marks in “generacōe” on lines 3 and 4 are retained approximately.
The final “con” on line 6 and initial “tra?” on line 7 are physically separate; they may form a divided word, but the transcription retains the break.
Only one continuous text area is visible. No separate marginal addition can be securely distinguished. There is a long oblique stroke near the right edge of line 6; I cannot determine whether it is a writing flourish, correction mark, or unrelated mark. No overlapping crops were supplied.

Limitations
Line 1 is severely cropped; line 2 is faint and difficult to distinguish. The bottom of line 8 is cropped. Brown discoloration, low contrast, crowded letterforms, and overwriting limit this reading, especially lines 2, 4, 6, and 7. Several words may be misread. I have left unreadable text and uncertain readings visible rather than completing sentences from their apparent sense.
